audit.whatIsWrong: The content win array gives Akshan levels 1-5, but whys[2] says "Garen edges 3" and whys[3] says "He stays ahead at 4-5", directly contradicting the chart they sit next to. whys[5] says "Garen takes the first-item window" on a stage marked Skill. In the full layer, Level 6 (Garen), First item (Skill) and 2+ items (Skill) all carried Akshan-favoured boilerplate.
audit.why: Garen has no ranged tool at all, so Avengerang at 850 and the Dirty Fighting second shot genuinely own levels 1-5 — the chart is right and the whys were wrong. The lane turns at 6 when Demacian Justice arrives, which is exactly where the chart marks Garen.
audit.corrected: whys 2, 3 and 5 rewritten to argue for their own side, and the three contradicted full-layer stages now give the real reason: the R answering yours at 6, Stridebreaker sticking at first item, and a tankier Garen out-sustaining the duel at two.

audit.why: The four spikes are the right ones: Akshan at 1, Garen at 2-3 with Decisive Strike and Courage, Youmuu's versus Stridebreaker at first item, and Demacian Justice (120/100/80) at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Courage's tenacity is given as a reason to fear the ability in three strings — "grants tenacity, blanking the kite your whole kill pattern relies on", "the tenacity shrugs off your slow", "the tenacity shrugs off the only slow you have". Neither Courage's nor Decisive Strike's cooldown appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Akshan has no slow and no crowd control of any kind, so Courage's tenacity does nothing whatsoever in this matchup — the half that matters is the shield and the lesser damage reduction that follows it, on 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s. Pointing the reader at tenacity makes them mis-read which part of the ability to play around. Decisive Strike being a flat 8s is the single most useful number in the lane, because it is the gap you chip in.
audit.corrected: Tenacity is now named as dead weight against your kit in the one place it belongs, and the surrounding advice keys off Courage's 22s shield-plus-reduction and Decisive Strike's flat 8s silence instead.

edits.before: Chip him off the wave and swing away from everything he commits. Keep one eye on Courage and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Chip him off the wave and swing away from everything he commits. Decisive Strike is a flat 8s — that silence is the clock.

edits.before: Garen wins by landing Courage, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Garen wins by silencing your cast with Decisive Strike, spinning you up in Judgment, and executing what is left.

edits.before: Trade on his CS timings and bank the passive shield-sprints. Track Courage; the swing dies to one good answer.
edits.after: Trade on his CS timings and bank the passive shield-sprints. Courage is 22s at rank 1 — burst in its downtime.

edits.before: Comeuppance online — the lock-on execute closes everything you chip. Scoundrels die; teammates revive.
edits.after: Demacian Justice answers yours: he silences with Q, then executes — never trade at 6 with his R up.

edits.before: First item spike — the swing-fire pattern now removes half bars. Take over the lane and start roaming for revives.
edits.after: Youmuu's lands, but Stridebreaker lets him close and stick — commit only while Decisive Strike is on its 8s.

edits.before: Crit items even out the field — your edge stays the map game: revives, executes, and swings nobody wards.
edits.after: A tankier Garen out-sustains the duel — pick and roam instead: camo W, R from range, and the takedown reset.

edits.before: - Garen Courage: matchup-defining — Damage reduction on cast — your burst only lands full once it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E swing has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Garen Courage: matchup-defining — 22s at rank 1: a shield and tenacity first, then lesser damage reduction. Burst once it is down. - Your E swing has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

edits.before: Damage reduction on cast — your burst only lands full once it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: 22s at rank 1: a shield, then lesser damage reduction. Your burst only lands full once it is down — wait for it.

edits.before: Track Garen’s Courage: Damage reduction on cast — your burst only lands full once it is down. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Garen’s Courage: 22s at rank 1 — a shield and tenacity first, then lesser damage reduction. Your burst only lands full in its downtime.

edits.before: Garen's window: once he points Q (Decisive Strike) it silences your next cast and lands an empowered, slowing strike, and W (Courage) shaves your burst and gives tenacity. If he closes and silences you mid-Q-or-E, you eat the full melee trade animation-locked.
edits.after: Garen's window: once he points Q (Decisive Strike) — a flat 8s — it silences your next cast and lands an empowered, slowing strike, and W (Courage) shields and blunts your burst for 22s. If he silences you mid-Q-or-E, you eat the whole melee trade.

edits.before: Pop W (Courage) as you burst so your damage hits reduced and the tenacity shrugs off your slow, then spin you with E
edits.after: Pop W (Courage) as you burst so the shield and damage reduction eat it, then spin you up with E (Judgment)

edits.before: Garen edges 3: W (Courage) eats your burst with damage reduction and grants tenacity, blanking the kite your whole kill pattern relies on.
edits.after: You still own 3: Courage's shield and damage reduction blunt your burst for 22s, but its tenacity does nothing — you carry no CC to shrug.

edits.before: He stays ahead at 4-5 — his raw bruiser stats and Q-silence out-trade you up close, so you can only chip, never commit into his Q.
edits.after: You hold 4-5 by spacing — his raw stats win up close, but Decisive Strike is a flat 8s, so chip in that gap and never commit into it.

edits.before: Even at 6: your R can execute a chipped Garen from range, but his Demacian Justice true-damage execute answers back the instant he silences you with Q.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: Demacian Justice answers your channel and the Q silence lands first, so never fight at 6 with his ult up and yours down.

edits.before: Garen takes the first-item window — Stridebreaker's dash-and-slow lets him close and stick through your swing, outpacing your lethality if his Q is up.
edits.after: It's on execution at first item — Stridebreaker lets him close and stick, so your Youmuu's spike only converts while Decisive Strike is on its flat 8s.

edits.before: By 3 Garen has W (Courage), so your burst window shrinks — he pops the damage reduction as you commit and the tenacity shrugs off the only slow you have. The play is patience: chip him off the wave so his untargeted passive regen never ticks, and hold E to swing off a wall the instant he throws Q so the silence whiffs instead of locking your cast. He out-trades you up close on raw bruiser stats here, so don't duel into his Q — duel into his Q cooldown. At 6 his Demacian Justice is a true-damage execute that ignores your build, so even a chipped Garen can flip a trade by silencing you with Q and pressing R first.
edits.after: By 3 Garen has W (Courage), so your burst window shrinks — he pops the shield and damage reduction as you commit, though its tenacity is dead weight here because you carry no slow or CC for it to shrug off. The play is patience: chip him off the wave so his untargeted passive regen never ticks, and hold E to swing off a wall the instant he throws Q so the silence whiffs instead of locking your cast. Decisive Strike is a flat 8s, so you always know when the gap opens — don't duel into his Q, duel into its cooldown. At 6 his Demacian Justice ignores your build, so even a chipped Garen flips a trade by silencing you and pressing R first.

notes: The page describes Demacian Justice as missing-HP true damage in four places. Riot's description is only 'attempts to execute an enemy champion' with a trueDamage flag and no scaling stated, so I could not verify the missing-health scaling from the kit and left those strings alone rather than assert or delete. Logged as unverified. Courage's shield is worth noting separately: the kit gives shield plus tenacity on cast, then lesser damage reduction — the page had collapsed that into 'damage reduction on cast'.
